title: Whole Thick-Keeled Serrate-Leaf Rosette
description: One complete newly authored static succulent-like rosette. A small common basal crown supports directly rooted long tapering sword leaves: each is a true thick continuous closed volume with a shallow longitudinal upper channel, heavy lower keel and integral alternating toothed side margins. Lower leaves arch outward while a few smaller inner leaves rise upright; no separate thin petioles, broad oval pads, flat alpha planes or repeated floating edge spikes. The whole fleshy longitudinal section, toothed outline and direct crown assembly differ from old inflated-stalk floating oval rosette and branching flattened paddle cactus, not merely a leaf count or color variant. One whole plant prop zero scenes. No exact aloe/agave species, medicinal use, roots, growth, cultivation, water storage performance or ecological claim.
